raw_response:
I will do it much like last year, because on 12 mu I cannot afford to gamble. Around here, if wheat looks weak in spring or maize stays pale after it comes up, yield drops fast, and that hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I mostly follow what good growers nearby do and what I have seen work in our county with well water. For winter wheat, I will put the stronger fertilizer under before sowing, then topdress once when it starts growing hard in spring, and I will water about three times if the year is normal. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people do, give it enough base fertilizer plus one main nitrogen feeding, and water two times with the well if rain is not enough. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. Seed, fertilizer, water, spray, all cost money, but if the ears and cobs do not fill, then the whole year is wasted.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 12 mu and farm close to what has worked before in Quzhou. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I have seen those give steadier harvests. I will not cut fertilizer too much, because losing yield costs more than a few extra bags. For wheat I will feed it enough before sowing and again in spring, water about three times with my well, and spray two times if needed. For maize I will plant right after wheat, use enough nitrogen to keep it dark green, water about two times, and spray two times. I will stay with rotary tillage because it is what I know, it fits my labor, and it works on my land.
